text: The lab results show normal readings for your blood count, CRP, and urinalysis, which helps rule out sepsis and chorioamnionitis. Given the negative infectious workup, are you currently breastfeeding, and have you noticed any breast pain, redness, or hard lumps? This will help determine if you have developed mastitis.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis (likely retained products of conception), though the reported normal inflammatory markers and lack of breast symptoms make puerperal mastitis or sepsis less likely despite the fever.
